symptom: The guest-facing invitation was Hebrew while the product requirement was an explicit Hebrew or English meeting choice controlling all subsequent output.
expected_behavior: The organizer explicitly selects Hebrew or English before booking, and that choice controls the interface, default title, calendar description and branded guest email.
environment: SpaPlus Global production meeting route at https://app.spaplus.co/tools/meetings, version 202, authenticated Hebrew success state on 2026-08-23.

steps: Open the authenticated meeting route in production.
Inspect the language control and completed booking state.
Compare the visible control with the received branded invitation screenshot.
reproduction.evidence: The live DOM exposed only a small English interface toggle and no explicit meeting-language field; the supplied invitation screenshot rendered the entire guest message in Hebrew.

observations.observation: The existing header button changed activeLocale but was labelled only with the other interface language.
observations.evidence: MeetingClient.tsx before fix used one meeting-language header button calling setActiveLocale.

observations.observation: The default meeting title did not react to a language change.
observations.evidence: MeetingClient.tsx before fix used defaultValue derived from activeLocale on the uncontrolled title input.

observations.observation: The calendar description always ended in English.
observations.evidence: route.ts before fix appended Scheduled with SpaPlus Global regardless of locale.

hypotheses.mechanism: The API discards the selected locale before generating the branded email.
hypotheses.prediction: The request locale would be absent or brandedGuestEmail would have no locale branch.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Inspect request serialization and email generation branches.
hypotheses.result: The client sent locale: activeLocale and brandedGuestEmail already branched on data.locale.

hypotheses.mechanism: The product conflated interface switching with an explicit meeting-language decision and left generated defaults partially unbound to the selection.
hypotheses.prediction: The live form would have no explicit meeting-language field, the title would be uncontrolled and at least one generated calendar string would be fixed-language.
hypotheses.discriminating_test: Inspect the production DOM and the three generation boundaries in source.
hypotheses.result: All three predictions were observed: no language field, an uncontrolled default title and a constant English calendar signature.

fix.change: Add a prominent accessible Hebrew or English meeting-language selector, make the default title react safely to selection, and localize the calendar signature from the same locale used by the email generator.
fix.evidence: Commit 8aa403f adds the selector and one locale state controlling request payload, title defaults, calendar description and branded email.

affected_family: Branded guest email HTML, text and subject

regression_checks.check: Production build and full automated suite
regression_checks.evidence: Vinext production build passed and 76 tests passed with zero failures.
The new test verifies both language choices, locale request propagation, reactive default title, localized calendar signature and email language direction.
The account typography audit passed the complete clean worktree.

authorization_boundary: Targeted code repair and validation only; no new Google scopes, permissions or calendar data changes.
